text: SUM aggregates a column directly. Iterator functions do something different — they walk a table row by row. Here's SUMX, the one you'll reach for first.

Sometimes the number you need isn't a stored column at all — only Quantity and UnitPrice exist. SUMX evaluates Quantity times UnitPrice fresh for every row, then adds up the results. SUM alone has no way to express that.

And SUMX's table argument doesn't have to be the whole table — pair it with FILTER, and you sum a value across only the rows matching a condition. Here, every sale except the ones tied to the United States.

Every aggregation has an X-suffixed cousin, all following the same shape: iterate a table, evaluate an expression per row, combine the results. Reach for one whenever the value has to be calculated fresh, row by row, instead of already existing as a column.
Next: back to CALCULATE, for the filter-modifier functions that give it even finer control.
